memory.interpretation: Strong immediate state dependence is robust. The original older-history gain is reference-dependent: it is supported under geography/bay references but not after stable transect identity is added, indicating that long history partly proxies persistent among-transect heterogeneity rather than cleanly identifying a long biological memory horizon.

site_identity_audit.interpretation: Formal older-history support disappears for every state dimension when stable transect identity is added. The original long-history gain therefore partly reflects persistent site-specific heterogeneity not captured by coordinates and bay segment; node identity is a saturated reference, not an identified ecological mechanism.

quantitative_state.model: within-transect fixed effects; cyclic survey-day and log sampled-point-count adjustment; node-cluster bootstrap
quantitative_state.interpretation: Recorded presence and quantitative meadow condition are partly decoupled. This is a candidate cryptic-degradation/state-decoupling result, not yet an environmental-causal result.

pulse_2016_2017.survey_date_warning: 24/47 eligible 2016 visits use 2016-12-25; four of five pulse nodes use this date.
pulse_2016_2017.effort_warning: Pulse-node 2016/2015 sampled-point ratios range from 0.854 to 3.545.
pulse_2016_2017.date_semantics_warning: Pinned OBIS conversion uses minimum date within IDall, while current tbeptools read_formtransect uses maximum date for multi-day samples.

claim_boundary: Do not equate recorded presence/non-detection with demographic occupancy/extinction.
Do not interpret the 2016/2017 pulse as a confirmed ecological disturbance until original survey-date/protocol semantics are resolved.
Braun-Blanquet values are ordinal abundance classes, not percent cover.
Blade length and shoot density are secondary because measurement coverage is incomplete.
Current environmental associations are descriptive; no climate-causal attribution is supported.
Do not select a nominal annual water-quality association as a mechanism after inspecting the screen; no declared post-2016 association survives FDR control.
Do not add further retrospective seasonal windows to rescue the hot/fresh mechanism; both annual and predeclared 3/6-month screens are negative.
Quantitative early warning is internally walk-forward validated but was motivated after observing Tampa state decoupling; external or untouched prospective confirmation is still required.
Do not retune or add another response-free mechanism simulation family after the frozen latent-occupancy v1 hard stop; the mechanism remains unresolved.
Do not present the original binary older-history gain as a robust long biological-memory result after the stable-node reference audit; formal support disappears when node identity is added.
Do not interpret node_id as a causal habitat mechanism; it is a saturated repeated-site reference.

Do not infer that EOG prediction failure proves dispersal or connectivity is ecologically irrelevant; the post-hoc translation tests only static geometry and one simple annual neighborhood formulation.
Treat persistent site template, clonal buffering and local threshold loss as ecological hypotheses requiring direct habitat or demographic measurements, not identified causes.

Do not interpret the failed segment/neighborhood increments as proof that Tampa transects are ecologically independent; common forcing may act at other temporal scales or through unmeasured exposures.

lower_tampa_bay.interpretation: Consistent with compositional reorganization toward more frequent Halodule while Thalassia and Syringodium decline quantitatively; not proof of competition or replacement mechanism.

old_tampa_bay.interpretation: No strong monotone alternative-seagrass replacement; the stronger signal remains declining Thalassia blade length and shoot density.

middle_tampa_bay.interpretation: Thalassia and Syringodium year-to-year frequency changes are positively rather than negatively coupled; the stronger focal signal is declining Thalassia blade length.

community_reorganization.synthesis: Post-2016 degradation mode differs among bay segments rather than following one common Tampa-wide trajectory.

environmental_coupling.interpretation: No simple annual water-quality variable currently provides a multiplicity-controlled segment-year explanation of post-2016 state changes. Environmental causation remains unresolved; finer-scale stress mechanisms remain possible.

exposures: maximum monthly mean temperature over prior 3/6 months
minimum monthly mean salinity over prior 3/6 months
seasonal_hot_fresh_screen.interpretation: Aligning hot/fresh exposure to 3- and 6-month pre-survey windows does not recover a multiplicity-controlled association with Thalassia frequency or Braun-Blanquet state change. Acute/finer-scale mechanisms remain unresolved.

quantitative_early_warning.endpoint: next-year recorded Thalassia loss among source-year recorded-positive stable transects

target_2016.interpretation: Retained in the primary result as an adverse year; exclusion is sensitivity only.

quantitative_early_warning.interpretation: Source-year quantitative meadow state adds strict out-of-time information about next-year recorded loss beyond space, year, survey timing and sampled-point effort. This supports an early-warning hypothesis for recorded-state instability, not demographic extinction risk.

nps_quantitative_memory.interpretation: The external NPS Zostera panel supports immediate previous-year quantitative state dependence beyond persistent site identity, but does not support a robust increment from older history beyond lag-1. This motivates a state-dependent memory-horizon hypothesis without establishing why Tampa binary state and NPS quantitative cover differ.

matched_state_dimension_memory.interpretation: Quantitative frequency and Braun–Blanquet state show strong previous-year dependence. The earlier apparent binary-versus-quantitative older-history contrast is weakened by a later reference-saturation audit: once stable node identity is added, no state dimension has a supported older-history increment across the tested tau grid.

exponential_memory_operator_replay.interpretation: Transferring the exact exponential-memory representation family used by the binary Tampa analysis does not produce a supported older-history increment for either quantitative state. This reduces, but does not eliminate, representation choice as an explanation of the state-dimension contrast.

threshold_induced_memory_known_truth.interpretation: Lossy conversion of the same sampled quantitative frequency to binary detection was not sufficient to reproduce the Tampa-like older-history advantage under a first-order latent ecological process. This weakens a thresholding-only explanation but does not prove biological long-memory.

quantitative_memory_conditioning_audit.interpretation: Removing the persistent-presence restriction does not restore older-history value for quantitative frequency or Braun-Blanquet state.

two_timescale_hidden_state_memory_known_.interpretation: A slow latent AR(1) persistence/suitability process plus faster conditional condition is not sufficient, over the frozen grid, to reproduce the Tampa state-dimension memory pattern.

latent_occupancy_detection_memory_known_.hard_stop: Stop response-free mechanism hunting after this v1; do not retune this grid or add another simulation family in the same mechanism line.
latent_occupancy_detection_memory_known_.interpretation: First-order latent occupancy persistence plus imperfect detection produces some binary-biased older-history signal, especially under high occupancy persistence, but does not robustly reproduce the complete Tampa pattern.

eog_ecological_translation.interpretation: Occurrence, frequency and Braun-Blanquet levels are strongly anchored to persistent transect identity, whereas blade length and shoot density are much less site-saturated. A simple annually refreshed neighborhood state at the four frozen EOG radii does not add mean heldout predictive value beyond stable node identity and local lag-1. This favors a local-site-template/local-meadow-state working hypothesis over simple annual neighborhood-accessibility control.

dynamic_neighborhood_decomposition.interpretation: After stable node identity and own lag-1 state, neither previous-year water-body mean state nor local neighborhood deviation adds supported next-year predictive information for frequency or Braun-Blanquet state. The annual quantitative dynamics are therefore more consistent with site-local control than simple segment-wide synchrony or local spatial propagation at the tested scales.
